# Interaction concept (Bedienkonzept)

Cross-cutting rules for how NoteDown is operated, independent of a single
feature: layout per device tier (`PROJECT.md` → "Device tiers"), input,
feedback and the visual language. Feature-specific behavior stays in
`docs/requirements.md`; a rule moves here once a second feature needs it.

Current state, edited in place when a decision changes.

## Layout per tier

| | Phone (< 600 px) | Tablet (600–1023 px) | Desktop (≥ 1024 px) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top bar | Title; icons for search, sort, archive (count on its corner), Sync & sharing (sync status), Reminders, Export, ⋮ | Title, the search field right after it, then the same icons | Title; the search field centered over the notes, as wide as their cards; the same icons right of it |
| Table of contents and People (#23) | Bottom sheet whose handle peeks out at the bottom; tabs "Contents \| People", always | Fixed sidebar on the left, same tabs | Fixed sidebar on the left, same tabs |
| Note list | Cards, full width | Cards next to the sidebar | Cards next to the sidebar, at most 780 px wide |
| Search | Icon turns the top bar into a search field; with a text it shows the hit counter and ▲ / ▼ | Always visible field, wider with a text for the counter and ▲ / ▼ | Always visible field, counter and ▲ / ▼ inside |
| Multi-select | Contextual top bar: ✕, count, main action icons, rest under ⋮; the contents handle stays | Contextual top bar: ✕, count, action icons | Same, actions with labels |
| Panels (Sync & sharing, share dialog) | Full-screen sheet with ✕ / back | Centered dialog, max 480 px | Centered dialog, max 480 px |

- **Top bar actions** are icons with a tooltip; sort shows its label
  when there is room. Whatever doesn't fit goes under ⋮, with its icon,
  from the right end: Export first, then Reminders, Sync & sharing,
  archive, sort (the label goes before any button). Both views keep the
  same buttons, so the view button keeps its place. ⋮ holds what didn't
  fit, the theme and the prototype's tools.
- One primary action per view, as a floating button: + at the bottom
  right in the main view; in the archive it moves to the bottom left and
  turns into the red bin that empties the archive (in the trash the same
  bin deletes the selected notes permanently, greyed out without a
  selection and kept visible while selecting — far from Restore in the
  selection bar) (animated, during a
  swipe between the views in step with the finger; left, so it is never
  taken for +). The snackbar then sits right of it.
- The app draws edge-to-edge: top bars, the sidebar and full-screen
  panels extend their background behind the system status bar and keep
  their controls below it, bottom elements stay above the gesture bar
  (safe-area insets; Android forces edge-to-edge from version 15).
- The archive keeps the main view's layout; only the background tint, the
  title and the view button tell them apart: "Archive" in the main view
  turns into "Notes" in the archive, in the same place and size right
  after sort, so one tap switches back and
  forth (decided 2026-10-13 over a back button at the left). On touch
  devices the archive also lies to the right of the notes (see "Input").
- The phone keeps bottom elements clear of the contents handle: the +
  button and the snackbar sit above it.

## Input

- **Tap or click** is the main action on content: into a note's text =
  edit, on a task checkbox = toggle, on the round button (bottom right
  of the card) = close / reopen, on a link = open.
- **Long-press** is reserved for secondary modes: on a note, a
  heading in a note or a contents entry it starts multi-select, on + it starts dictation. Nothing essential is
  long-press-only on the desktop (Ctrl/Shift+click, a click on a card's
  frame outside its text, keyboard).
- **Selection mode** (multi-select): a contextual top bar replaces the
  normal one and the primary action button is hidden; a tap anywhere on
  an item toggles it, nothing inside the item acts. The note list and the
  contents share one selection, and the user can switch between them
  while selecting. The back button and
  `Esc` leave the mode first. A selected item is marked by the accent
  border only; a selected part of an item by an accent tint.
- Touch screens: rendered notes don't offer native text selection or
  the long-press callout, so the long-press stays free for multi-select;
  text is selected in the editor or copied with Copy.
- **Swipe sideways** (phone and tablet) moves between the notes and the
  archive, which lies to their right, like pages (the trash lies right of
  the archive, but a swipe only leads out of it, never in): it starts anywhere on
  the list or the contents (also the open sheet); the list follows the
  finger and the other view's page moves in beside it; let go past half
  the width or with a flick, it snaps onto the other view, otherwise
  back; past either end it only gives a little. The contents list
  where it shows (sidebar, open sheet) moves along in step, the other
  view's contents moving in beside it; the top bar and the contents' head
  stay in place (an open sheet stays open) and are refilled once the view
  has switched, but their background tint (also the closed sheet's)
  moves with the pages, split where the two views meet, in one straight
  line with them also in a flick. The whole screen below the top bar takes the
  swipe, also below the last card. Not while editing,
  selecting or recording; content that scrolls sideways itself (a wide
  table) keeps the gesture. Desktop has no touch, the view button
  switches there.
- **Bottom sheets** (phone) have a handle: a tap opens fully or closes.
  The whole sheet is one surface: dragging it anywhere leaves it at any
  height, past the top it slides out at the top instead of scrolling
  inside; an upward flick opens a closed sheet fully and glides on an
  open one, a downward flick or a drag near the bottom closes. A closed
  sheet is also pulled up (or flicked open) by a drag up from a thin
  strip at either screen edge in the bottom third.
- **Back** (Android button or gesture) closes the innermost layer first:
  a dialog or panel page, the selection, the editor (editing ends), the
  open contents sheet; only then does it leave the app. Each layer sits
  on its own history entry. The trash counts as such a layer: back from it
  goes to the archive.
- **Pull to refresh** (phone and tablet, while sync is on): pulling the
  list down from its top syncs now; a round indicator follows the finger
  and spins until the sync is over. Desktop syncs by opening Sync &
  sharing instead.
- No hover-only controls: everything reachable with the mouse is also
  visible and reachable by touch. Touch targets are at least 44 px
  (task checkboxes get an enlarged invisible target).
- **Editing** happens in place: the tapped note turns into the editor,
  the rest of the list stays as it is. One note is edited at a time;
  any tap outside it ends the edit first and then does what it would
  have done. While editing, the + button gives way to the toolbar.
- Controls that act on the editor (toolbar, its menus) never take the
  focus, so the on-screen keyboard stays open.
- The **caret stays visible** while editing: when the on-screen keyboard
  opens, and while typing, the list scrolls so the edited line sits
  between the top bar and the toolbar above the keyboard, with up to three
  lines of context above and below it where there is room (an edited line
  at the very edge loses what it continues).
- Editing ends only on a tap or click that **starts** outside the note: a
  text selection dragged out of the note keeps editing and the selection.
- **Hold-to-record** follows Signal: hold the + button (350 ms) to start,
  release to finish, slide left to cancel, slide up onto the lock to
  record hands-free — then the button turns into a check to finish and a
  bin appears to cancel. A level bar, the elapsed time and the live
  transcript show that it is listening. Short vibration on start, lock
  and cancel where the device supports it.
- The list never reorders while the user works in it — only after
  view, sort or search changes, and when a new due date sorts its note
  in under the due-date sort; that note then keeps its place on the
  screen (`docs/requirements.md` → "Sorting").
- Keyboard on the desktop: `n` new note, `/` search (Enter / Shift+Enter
  next / previous hit), `Esc` ends editing,
  closes menus, panels and dialogs and ends multi-select; Markdown shortcuts in the editor
  (`docs/requirements.md` → "Creating and editing").

## Feedback and undo

- Changes that remove a note from view (close, reopen, merge, an emptied
  note) happen immediately and offer **Undo** in a snackbar for 5
  seconds instead of asking for confirmation first.
- **Delete moves into the trash** (Delete in the selection) at once,
  with Undo: nothing is lost, the trash keeps it for 30 days
  (`docs/requirements.md` → "Main view, archive and trash").
- **Final and mass deletes ask first** (Empty archive, Delete
  permanently in the trash), and so does **Clear done tasks** although its
  tasks only move to the archive (person-requested; accent-colored
  button): the dialog says what goes, its action button is
  red, Cancel / `Esc` / back close it; Undo still follows for 5 seconds
  (decided 2026-10-14; Delete itself no longer asks since 2026-10-15).
- **Giving a trashed note back to others asks first** (Restore for …):
  it reaches people who deleted the note. Same dialog with an
  accent-colored action button; Undo follows (decided 2026-10-15, user
  request).
- Other confirmation dialogs only where the user has something to
  adjust: the order for Copy and Merge (drag an entry's grip; Merge shows
  it even for a single part, as the confirmation of what moves), the
  people for Share.
- Panels with several pages (Sync & sharing) go one page back with the
  back button, `Esc` or the system back gesture, and close from the
  first page; the primary button of a page (on the Sync & sharing
  overview: the sync status) sits in a footer that stays visible.

## Visual language

- Colors: Catppuccin flavors mapped to semantic tokens (`app/css/app.css`
  top): surfaces from `base`/`mantle`, text from `text`/`subtext`,
  accent Mauve, overdue = red, done = green, links = blue; the archive
  tints the surfaces with teal.
- Status marks: a **round** button for the note itself, **square**
  checkboxes for tasks inside the text.
- People are shown as **initials avatars**, each contact in one stable
  color from a set of six Catppuccin colors (peach, teal, blue, green,
  pink, yellow).
- Editing looks like reading: the live preview uses the same type sizes
  and list layout as the rendered note, so entering edit mode doesn't
  make the note jump; only the line with the cursor shows its Markdown.
- Recording is red (Catppuccin `red`): the + button, the blinking dot and
  the active microphone in the toolbar.
- Dates are shown relative where it helps ("Today 08:40", "Yesterday"),
  otherwise as "12 Oct"; the meta line under a note shows the date the
  list is sorted by.
